title: What Changed
summary: Latest curated deltas from the overnight research pass. The main change is not a new AI-infra thesis, but stronger evidence inside the physical bottleneck stack.

entries.title: Memory and optics evidence strengthened; power and packaging stayed confirmed
entries.whatChanged: Memory gained broader DRAM shortage quantification, with Nikkei reporting planned output increases may meet only about 60% of demand through around 2027. Optics gained more specific InP / 1.6T supply-chain pressure evidence.
entries.thesisImpact: The AI physical bottleneck thesis strengthened. The edge is increasingly threshold evidence inside the bottleneck stack rather than another generic claim that AI infrastructure is tight.
entries.expressionImpact: No expression ranking changed yet. Memory scarcity is more convincing, but Samsung remains the more valuation-sane memory expression while SK Hynix is the cleaner but more crowded HBM scarcity exposure.
entries.followUp: Pull Coherent, Lumentum, AAOI, Credo, Broadcom, and Keysight commentary for explicit 800G/1.6T lead-time, utilization, optical-test, and bring-up friction language.

entries.title: Liquid cooling is stronger as a narrative, but still threshold-gated
entries.whatChanged: Brownfield retrofit commentary increased, but named scaled retrofit-order evidence from hyperscalers and colocation operators is still missing.
entries.thesisImpact: Cooling remains a real constraint, but the public-market expression needs more proof that retrofit adoption becomes a direct revenue/margin driver rather than just a data-center architecture talking point.
entries.expressionImpact: Keep cooling-exposed names in the pullback-only / monitor bucket unless customer order evidence improves.
entries.followUp: Search operator disclosures for named brownfield liquid-cooling retrofit orders at Equinix, Digital Realty, CoreWeave, Microsoft, Meta, Oracle, and HPE.

entries.title: Bottleneck conviction and fresh-entry attractiveness are diverging
entries.whatChanged: The stronger bottleneck evidence did not automatically make every related equity attractive at current prices.
entries.thesisImpact: The AI theme remains real, but the House View should distinguish thesis quality from expression quality.
entries.expressionImpact: Use valuation-sane expression maps and ticker movement context before chasing second-order AI beneficiaries.
entries.followUp: Refresh the memory/HBM and power-equipment watchlist after material price moves or fresh earnings commentary.
